messages:
alice: Quick sync — noticed flaky e2e around streaming timeouts. Node SDK calls hang when request times out but stream still open. Repro steps in thread. Anyone seen this? @ben @carla
ben: Saw that yesterday. Node streaming uses AbortController but our http2 adapter doesn't forward the signal in the read loop. I can repro with a small script.
carla: Python differs: our httpx async client cancels the request but the generator keeps yielding cached chunks unless you close the response explicitly. Using `async with client.stream(...)` usually helps.
dmitri: Go: passing ctx cancels the request but our server stream handler continues to write if it doesn't check ctx.Done(); leaked goroutines are possible.
ben: Quick repro for Node:

```
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 2000);
const res = await client.stream({ model: 'x', input: '...' , signal: ac.signal });
for await (const chunk of res) { console.log(chunk); }
```

If you abort, the `for await` never resolves sometimes (http2). I've got a small patch that wires the signal to the http2 session read loop.
carla: For Python test case I used:

```
async with client.stream(...) as s:
    try:
        async for ch in s:
            pass
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        await s.aclose()
```

If you don't `aclose()` the transport drains later and test times out.
alice: OK good context. Action items: ben, can you open PR for Node patch + unit test? carla, can you add a small async test harness for Python and doc note about `aclose()`? dmitri, can you add a check in Go server handler to observe ctx.Done() and exit write loop? I'll add an e2e that runs the three harnesses to our flaky test job.
ben: Yep I'll do PR today. I'll add a deterministic e2e using a short-lived http2 server in CI to validate abort semantics.
ci-bot: build/1248 failed: flaky-e2e/streaming-timeout — https://ci.redwood/1248
carla: FYI also saw one more weirdness: retry logic can reattach a new stream without propagating previous aborts; recommend we tie retry attempts to a single AbortSignal/ctx so cancels apply across retries.
dmitri: Agreed. In Go I've modelled retries to create a child ctx and cancel parent cancels children; will push a small helper in runtime.
alice: Nice. Let's sync in tomorrow's standup for rollout. Thanks everyone :thumbsup: 
ben: marking this as follow-up, will tag PR with `devex:abort-timeout` and add reviewers @alice @carla
carla: will file a docs note in /docs/sdk/timeout-cancellation.md once tests pass.
alice: Perfect, closing the loop.
